entities.name: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks
entities.description: An iOS app that prompts office workers to take brief guided movement breaks at configurable intervals through the workday, and tracks what they complete.

hasChunks.text: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks is an iOS mobile app published by Mithul Mistry (bundle ID: com.mithulmistry.exercisesnacks ) that helps office workers interrupt prolonged sitting with brief, guided movement breaks — called "exercise snacks" — throughout the workday.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

hasChunks.text: Exercise Snacks prompts users to take short movement breaks at configurable intervals throughout their workday, guides them through a bodyweight exercise, and tracks their progress over time.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

hasChunks.text: Timer apps remind you to stand; Exercise Snacks guides you through specific, science-backed exercises with animated demonstrations, tracks your progress, and explains the research behind each movement.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

entities.name: Mithul Mistry
entities.description: Independent developer who publishes Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks.

hasChunks.text: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks is an independent iOS app published by Mithul Mistry. The app is available on the Apple App Store.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

entities.name: Exercise snack
entities.description: A brief bout of vigorous activity, under five minutes, repeated through the day rather than performed as a single session.

hasChunks.text: The "exercise snack" concept — brief vigorous bouts under 5 minutes, repeated throughout the day — has moved from niche curiosity to mainstream exercise science. The app's core recommendation (10 bodyweight squats every 45 minutes) is based on a direct randomized trial.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

hasChunks.text: Brief, targeted movement breaks — done consistently — produce measurable metabolic and cardiovascular benefits, even in people who exercise regularly outside work hours.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

entities.name: Bodyweight squat
entities.description: The app's hero exercise: a large-muscle bodyweight movement requiring no equipment, performed at or beside a desk.

hasChunks.text: Squats activate your largest muscle groups, stimulating protein synthesis and countering the muscle loss linked to prolonged sitting.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

hasChunks.text: Feet about shoulder-width, push your hips back as though reaching for a chair behind you, keep your chest up, stand back up. Ten of them takes about thirty seconds.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Desk exercises that actually do something

relations.targetName: Desk exercises that actually do something

entities.name: Prolonged sitting
entities.description: Extended uninterrupted sitting during the working day, and the metabolic and musculoskeletal effects attributed to it.

hasChunks.text: Sitting for long stretches raises blood sugar, stiffens muscles, and strains your heart. But you don't need a gym session to fight back.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

hasChunks.text: Hold any posture long enough and your body adapts to it. The muscles at the front of your chest and hips shorten. The ones across your upper back and backside stop doing much at all.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Posture exercises for people who sit all day

relations.targetName: Posture exercises for people who sit all day
Desk stretches you can do without leaving your chair

entities.name: Postprandial blood glucose
entities.description: Blood sugar level after eating; the primary outcome in the research the publisher cites for movement breaks.

hasChunks.text: Short squat breaks after meals blunt glucose and insulin spikes — the same effect as a 30-minute walk, without leaving your desk.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

hasChunks.text: Key finding: Quadriceps EMG amplitude is the strongest predictor of glucose clearance, meaning large-muscle contraction — regardless of whether from walking or squatting — drives the metabolic benefit.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

entities.name: Desk worker
entities.description: Office and knowledge workers who spend most of the working day seated; the app's primary audience.

hasChunks.text: Primary user: Office workers and knowledge workers who spend most of their working day seated — developers, designers, writers, analysts, managers — who know sitting too long is harmful but find it difficult to build a consistent movement habit.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

entities.name: Ten squats every 45 minutes
entities.description: The publisher's core protocol: ten bodyweight squats repeated at 45-minute intervals through the working day, taken from a 2024 randomised trial.

hasChunks.text: A 2024 randomized trial found that 10 bodyweight squats every 45 minutes reduced post-meal blood glucose by 21% — identical to frequent walking breaks, and nearly double the benefit of a single 30-minute walk.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

hasChunks.text: Ten squats. Forty-five minutes later, ten more. That's it. The most evidence-backed thing you'll do today.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

context.condition: ten bodyweight squats every 45 minutes; the reported effect is a 21% reduction in post-meal levels

entities.name: Exercise categories
entities.description: The publisher's four-way classification of its exercise library: Strength, Stretch, Cardio and Balance.

hasChunks.text: 30-Exercise Guided Library. Exercises span four categories: Strength, Stretch, Cardio, and Balance. The hero exercise is the bodyweight squat, supported by dedicated UI treatments, science callouts, and specific progress tracking. 8 exercises are free; 22 are Premium.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

hasChunks.text: Strength, Stretch, Cardio, and Balance — every break tailored to how you're feeling. Squats are always first: the most research-backed desk exercise you can do.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

entities.name: Break modes
entities.description: The publisher's three named break schedules — Focus, Balanced and Active — which set how often the app prompts a movement break.

hasChunks.text: Smart Break Reminders. Three notification modes — Focus (every 45 min), Balanced (every 30 min), and Active (every 20 min) — let users match break frequency to their work style. Reminders are local and privacy-respecting; no account required.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

hasChunks.text: Choose a rhythm that fits your day. Every mode keeps squats in the rotation — because the research says they're non-negotiable.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

entities.name: Compassionate Progress Tracking
entities.description: The publisher's named approach to progress tracking, in which missed days do not break a streak and any completed snack counts toward the daily goal.

hasChunks.text: Compassionate Progress Tracking. A flexible streak system, snack counter, and milestone badges celebrate consistency without punishing misses. Any completed exercise snack counts toward the daily goal — no guilt-driven mechanics.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

entities.name: Premium Annual
entities.description: The publisher's annual subscription, which unlocks the full exercise library, all break modes and full progress history.

hasChunks.text: Premium Annual £49.99 /year All 30 exercises, full progress history, streak tracking, milestone badges, and all future exercises added to the library. Subscriptions managed via RevenueCat. Payments handled through the Apple App Store.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks — AI Info & Brand Reference

hasChunks.text: Start free with 8 exercises — including squats, the science-backed hero. Unlock the full library and all three break modes when you're ready.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks — Move more, one snack at a time

entities.name: Apple Health
entities.description: Apple's health data platform. Completed exercise sessions are written to it as workout entries, with the user's permission.

hasChunks.text: With your permission, Exercise Snacks can write workout data to Apple Health. Specifically: When you complete an exercise, the app saves a workout entry (type, start time, duration, and estimated calories burned) to Apple Health on your device. We do not read any data from Apple Health.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Privacy Policy — Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks

entities.name: RevenueCat
entities.description: Third-party service used to manage in-app purchases and subscriptions.

hasChunks.text: RevenueCat Used to manage in-app purchases and subscriptions. When you make a purchase, RevenueCat processes transaction data on your behalf. No purchase is processed by us directly.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Privacy Policy — Exercise Snacks: Desk Breaks

entities.description: The React Native toolchain the app is built with.

hasChunks.text: Currently iOS only. The app is built with Expo (React Native), which supports Android, and Android availability may come in a future release.

entities.name: Posture exercises for people who sit all day
entities.description: A guide covering the four musculoskeletal patterns prolonged sitting creates, and the movements that counter each.

hasChunks.text: Most posture advice tells you to sit up straight. That is not a plan, because the problem is not how you sit for one minute. It is sitting in one position for eight hours.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Posture exercises for people who sit all day

hasChunks.text: What does change things is moving often. The exercises below target the four patterns that long sitting creates, and they are grouped that way rather than as a random list of stretches.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Posture exercises for people who sit all day

entities.name: Desk stretches you can do without leaving your chair
entities.description: A guide of ten stretches grouped by the area that aches, with a 60-second minimum version.

hasChunks.text: You do not need a mat, a change of clothes, or for anyone to notice. Most of what follows can be done in a chair, at a desk, in an open-plan office, without drawing attention.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Desk stretches you can do without leaving your chair

hasChunks.text: Every 30 to 60 minutes is a reasonable target. Not because stretching needs that frequency, but because sitting is the thing you are interrupting.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Desk stretches you can do without leaving your chair

entities.name: Desk exercises that actually do something
entities.description: A guide of strength and cardio movements for the workday, including three that are invisible in an open-plan office.

hasChunks.text: Stretching makes sitting more comfortable. Exercise changes what sitting does to you. They are not the same thing, and if you only have a minute a few times a day, this is the one worth spending it on.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Desk exercises that actually do something

hasChunks.text: Everything below takes between 30 and 75 seconds, needs no equipment beyond a chair or a desk, and can be done in work clothes.
hasChunks.pageTitle: Desk exercises that actually do something
